mainTopic: What happens to the body and soul after death: awareness, purity, the fate of צדיקים, בינונים and רשעים, and bodily decay
overview: This amud opens with the end of a story: רב יהודה made sure a man with no mourners was comforted during שבעה, and the man thanked him in a dream. רבי אבהו then teaches that the dead know what is said in front of them until the grave is closed. רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי disagree about how long that awareness lasts, and each one brings a פסוק. A ברייתא teaches that the soul must be returned to הקב״ה as pure as it was given, and it uses a parable of a king who lent out royal garments. רבי אליעזר adds that the souls of צדיקים are stored under the כסא הכבוד, while the souls of רשעים are slung back and forth. שמואל adds that בינונים go to דומה but have rest. רב מרי says even צדיקים turn to dust, and a story about the buried רב אחאי בר יאשיה shows that a person free of קנאה stays whole until one hour before תחיית המתים. Finally, רבי אבהו answers a מין: שמואל could be brought up by the בעלת אוב because it was within twelve months of his death. That ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב יהודה comforts a man who had no mourners
steps.stepSummary: Every day of the שבעה, רב יהודה gathered ten people to sit in the dead man's house. Afterward, the dead man appeared in a dream and thanked him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Every day רב יהודה would take a group of ten people, and they would sit in the dead man's place. After seven days, the dead man appeared to רב יהודה in a dream and said: 'May your mind be at rest, because you put my mind at rest.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story. A man died with no one to mourn him, so רב יהודה brought a מנין each day of the שבעה to sit in his house, and the man came in a dream to thank him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that the dead man knew people were sitting שבעה for him and was comforted by it. This leads straight into the next step, which asks how much the dead actually know about what happens around them.

keyTerms.meaning: In his place (the dead man's house)
May your mind be at rest

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how valuable it is to sit שבעה and comfort mourners, especially for a מת with no one of his own. The dead are actually helped by it.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יוֹמָא הֲוָה דָּבַר רַב יְהוּדָה בֵּי עַשְׂרָה,
phrases.english: Every day Rav Yehuda would take a group of ten
phrases.notes: During the seven days of mourning

phrases.english: and they would sit in his place.
phrases.notes: In the house of the man who died

phrases.english: After seven days
the dead man appeared to Rav Yehuda in his dream
and said to him:
May your mind be at rest, for you put my mind at rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל יוֹמָא הֲוָה דָּבַר רַב יְהוּדָה בֵּי עַשְׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a story that began in the previous part of the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Comforting the mourners for a מת with no mourners gives real comfort to the dead person himself.

steps.title: The dead know what is said in front of them
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו teaches that a מת knows everything said in his presence until the גולל is closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Everything people say in front of the dead person, he knows, until the grave is sealed with the גולל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a new rule: the dead person is aware of what people say around him, but only up to a certain point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule has two parts. The first part says the מת is aware of what is said. The second part sets a limit: this awareness lasts only until the grave is closed. That time limit is what the next step will argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of the dead person
That it is sealed or closed

steps.confusionAlert: Translators explain the word גולל in different ways. Some call it the top-stone of the tomb. תוספות explain it as the covering of the grave. Either way, it means the moment the burial is finished.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the reason we must be careful about what we say near a מת before burial. It is also why it matters what is said in a הספד.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Everything that people say in front of the dead, he knows,
until the grave covering is sealed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the story's message (the dead are aware) into a general rule with a time limit
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מת knows what is said in front of him until the גולל is sealed.

steps.title: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי disagree about how long the awareness lasts
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי argue about the time limit. One says it lasts until the grave is closed. The other says it lasts until the flesh decomposes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי disagree about this. One says the dead person is aware until the grave is sealed. The other says he is aware until the flesh decomposes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a מחלוקת about the end point of the dead person's awareness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that the מת is aware of what is said. They disagree only about when that awareness stops. The first opinion matches רבי אבהו. The second opinion gives the מת a much longer time of awareness, all the way until the body breaks down.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not tell us which of the two holds which opinion. It only says 'חד אמר' and 'וחד אמר', meaning 'one said' and 'the other said.'

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi disagree about this.
One said: until the grave covering is sealed,
and one said: until the flesh decomposes.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי אבהו's time limit is a matter of dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opinion 1: the awareness lasts until the גולל is sealed. Opinion 2: it lasts until the flesh decomposes.

steps.title: Source for the view that awareness lasts until the flesh decomposes
steps.stepSummary: The opinion of 'until the flesh decomposes' is based on a פסוק in איוב: his flesh feels pain and his soul mourns over it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says the awareness lasts until the flesh decomposes bases it on the פסוק: 'But his flesh grieves for him, and his soul mourns over him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the Scriptural source for the second opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the soul mourns over the flesh. This means the soul still feels what is happening to the body in the grave. As long as there is flesh to feel pain, the מת is aware.

phrases.english: The one who says: until the flesh decomposes,
is based on what is written: 'But his flesh grieves for him,'
'and his soul mourns over him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר עַד שֶׁיִּתְעַכֵּל הַבָּשָׂר, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the second opinion in the מחלוקת
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that the dead are aware until the flesh decomposes
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 14:22: 'His flesh grieves for him and his soul mourns over him.' This shows the soul feels what happens to the body in the grave.

steps.title: Source for the view that awareness lasts until the grave is sealed
steps.stepSummary: The opinion of 'until the גולל is sealed' is based on a פסוק in קהלת: once the dust returns to the earth, the spirit returns to God.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says the awareness lasts until the grave is sealed bases it on the פסוק: 'And the dust returns to the earth as it was, and so on.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the Scriptural source for the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the body is buried, it has 'returned to the earth.' The rest of the פסוק then says 'the spirit returns to God.' This means that at burial the soul leaves and no longer knows what happens to the body.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on (the rest of the verse)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is actually in the part of the פסוק that is not quoted, hidden behind the word 'וגו׳': 'and the spirit returns to God who gave it.' The very next step quotes those words.

phrases.english: The one who says: until the grave covering is sealed,
is based on what is written: 'And the dust returns to the earth'
'as it was, and so on.'
phrases.notes: קהלת 12:7. The verse continues: 'and the spirit returns to God who gave it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר עַד שֶׁיִּסָּתֵם הַגּוֹלֵל, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the first opinion, completing the pair
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that the dead are aware until the grave is sealed
steps.raayaSupportSource: קהלת 12:7: once the dust returns to the earth (burial), the spirit returns to God.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees the dead are aware for some time. The מחלוקת is only whether the awareness ends at burial (קהלת) or when the flesh decomposes (איוב).

steps.title: Return the soul as pure as it was given
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'the spirit returns to God who gave it' to mean that you must return your soul in the same purity in which you received it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And the spirit returns to God who gave it.' This means: give it back to Him the way He gave it to you. He gave it to you in purity, so you too must return it in purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that takes the end of the same פסוק and draws a moral lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'who gave it' are read as a standard to meet: return it the same way it was given. Since a person's נשמה comes from God pure, his job in life is to keep it pure and return it that way.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'And the spirit returns to God'
'who gave it' —
give it to Him as He gave it to you;
in purity, so you too, in purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְהָרוּחַ תָּשׁוּב אֶל הָאֱלֹהִים אֲשֶׁר נְתָנָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the second half of the פסוק that step 5 hinted at with 'וגו׳' and teaches a new lesson from it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person must return his נשמה to God in the same purity in which he received it.

steps.title: Parable of the king's garments: the setup
steps.stepSummary: A king hands out royal garments to his servants. The wise ones store them carefully, and the foolish ones wear them for work.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a human king who gave out royal garments to his servants. The wise servants folded them and put them in a box. The foolish servants went and did work while wearing them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a משל to illustrate the ברייתא. This step only sets up the story. The outcome comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The royal garments stand for the pure נשמה. The two kinds of servants stand for two kinds of people: those who guard their soul and those who 'use it up' in everyday matters and get it dirty.

phrases.english: A parable of a king of flesh and blood
who distributed royal garments to his servants.
The wise ones among them
folded them and placed them in a box.
The foolish ones among them
went and did work in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the ברייתא's lesson with a parable
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two kinds of servants: those who guard the king's garments and those who wear them out.

steps.title: Parable of the king's garments: the king's reaction
steps.stepSummary: When the king asks for his garments back, the wise return them pressed and clean, and the foolish return them dirty. The king is happy with the wise and angry with the foolish.
steps.simpleTranslation: After some time the king asked for his garments back. The wise returned them pressed, and the foolish returned them dirty. The king was happy to greet the wise and angry to greet the foolish.
steps.whatsHappening: The משל reaches its outcome. Each group returns the garments in a different condition, and the king reacts to each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king 'asking for his garments' stands for death, when God takes back the נשמה. Whoever kept his soul pure is welcomed with joy, and whoever soiled it faces anger. The full explanation of the משל continues next.
steps.whatToRemember: The נשמה is a royal garment lent to us by God. At death He asks for it back, and we are judged by whether we return it clean.

phrases.english: After some time the king requested his garments.

phrases.aramaic: פִּקְחִין שֶׁבָּהֶן הֶחֱזִירוּם לוֹ כְּשֶׁהֵן מְגוֹהָצִין,
phrases.english: The wise among them returned them to him pressed,

phrases.aramaic: טִפְּשִׁין שֶׁבָּהֶן הֶחֱזִירוּם לוֹ כְּשֶׁהֵן מְלוּכְלָכִין.
phrases.english: the foolish among them returned them to him dirty.
The king was happy to greet the wise ones,
and angry to greet the foolish ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story part of the parable begun in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Garments returned clean bring the king's joy, and garments returned soiled bring his anger.

steps.title: The king's verdict on the wise and the foolish servants
steps.stepSummary: The king stores his clean garments and sends the wise servants home in peace. He sends the dirty garments to be washed and locks the foolish servants in prison.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the wise ones, the king said: Put my garments back in the storehouse, and let these servants go home in peace. About the foolish ones he said: Send my garments to the launderer, and lock these servants in prison.
steps.whatsHappening: The משל of the king's garments ends with the king's verdict. Each group of servants gets a different result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group gets two separate results: one for the garments and one for the servants themselves. The wise keep their freedom and the garments go into storage. The foolish are jailed and the garments need cleaning. This two-part ending sets up the coming comparison of body and soul.

phrases.english: About the wise ones he said:
Let my garments be put in the storehouse,
and let them go to their homes in peace.
And about the foolish ones he said:
Let my garments be given to the launderer,
and let them be locked up in prison.
phrases.notes: This is their punishment for using the king's garments for their own work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משל begun in steps 7 and 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wise servants go free in peace. The foolish servants are imprisoned.

steps.title: Applying the parable to the righteous
steps.stepSummary: Like the king, הקדוש ברוך הוא gives peace to the bodies of צדיקים and binds their souls in the bundle of life.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too הקדוש ברוך הוא: about the bodies of the righteous He says, 'He enters into peace, they rest on their beds.' About their souls He says, 'The soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the meaning of the משל (the נמשל), starting with צדיקים. Their body and their soul each receive a good result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The body matches the garment that goes into storage: it rests peacefully in the grave. The soul matches the wise servant who goes home in peace: it is kept safe with God. Each half of the king's verdict now has a פסוק to back it up.

keyTerms.meaning: The bundle of life, where souls are kept safe

phrases.english: So too the Holy One, Blessed be He,
about the bodies of the righteous says:
"He enters into peace,
they rest on their beds,"
and about their souls He says:
"And the soul of my lord shall be
bound in the bundle of life."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the wise servants' half of the משל to צדיקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bodies of צדיקים rest in peace, and their souls are kept safe in צרור החיים.

steps.title: Applying the parable to the wicked
steps.stepSummary: The bodies of רשעים have no peace, and their souls are flung away as if from a sling.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the bodies of the wicked He says, 'There is no peace, says ה׳, for the wicked.' About their souls He says, 'The souls of your enemies He shall sling out in the hollow of a sling.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the נמשל with the רשעים. They match the foolish servants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The body gets no rest, like the dirty garment sent off to be washed. The soul is thrown around, like the foolish servant locked in prison. Both פסוקים in this step are the mirror image of the פסוקים used for צדיקים.

keyTerms.meaning: He will sling it (throw it as with a sling)

phrases.aramaic: עַל גּוּפָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים הוּא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: About the bodies of the wicked He says:
"There is no peace, says the Lord, for the wicked,"
and about their souls He says:
"And the souls of your enemies
He shall sling out in the hollow of a sling."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 25:29, the second half of the same פסוק used for the righteous

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל גּוּפָן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite side of step 10, matching the foolish servants.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bodies of רשעים have no peace, and their souls are slung away.
steps.whatToRemember: Body = the garment. Soul = the servant. צדיקים are like the wise servants, and רשעים are like the foolish ones.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: souls of the righteous are stored under the Throne of Glory
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר: the souls of צדיקים are hidden away beneath the כסא הכבוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר says that the souls of the righteous are stored beneath the Throne of Glory, as it says, 'The soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life.'
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds detail about where the souls of צדיקים actually go. It uses the same פסוק as step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 only said the souls are 'bound in the bundle of life.' רבי אליעזר tells us where that bundle is: under the כסא הכבוד.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The souls of the righteous
are stored beneath the Throne of Glory,
as it is stated: "And the soul of my lord shall be
bound in the bundle of life."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the 'bundle of life' idea from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The souls of צדיקים are kept under the כסא הכבוד.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: souls of the wicked are slung across the world
steps.stepSummary: The souls of רשעים are restless. Two angels at opposite ends of the world throw them back and forth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The souls of the wicked keep being tied up and moving around. One angel stands at one end of the world and another angel stands at the other end, and they sling the souls to each other, as it says, 'The souls of your enemies He shall sling out in the hollow of a sling.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר continues and describes what happens to the souls of רשעים. He gives a picture of the 'sling' from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'sling' in the פסוק is read as an image: the soul is thrown back and forth and never finds a resting place. This is the opposite of the righteous souls, which are safely stored.

keyTerms.meaning: Continually tied up and moving about
They sling, throw back and forth

phrases.english: And those of the wicked are continually tied up and moving about,
and one angel stands at one end of the world,
and another angel stands at the other end of the world,
and they sling their souls to one another,
as it is stated: "And the souls of your enemies
He shall sling out in the hollow of a sling."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of רבי אליעזר's ברייתא, the opposite of step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The souls of רשעים are thrown back and forth and have no rest.

steps.title: רבה asks about people in between
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks רב נחמן what happens to the souls of בינונים, people who are neither righteous nor wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to רב נחמן: What about the in-between people?
steps.whatsHappening: We have heard about צדיקים and רשעים, so רבה asks about the middle group. This question sets up רב נחמן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא described only two groups. רבה points out a gap: most people fall somewhere in the middle, so where do their souls go?

keyTerms.meaning: In-between people, neither fully righteous nor wicked

phrases.english: Rabba said to Rav Naḥman:
What about those of the middling people?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a case the ברייתא left out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The fate of the souls of בינונים.

steps.title: רב נחמן quotes שמואל: middling souls go to דומה but have rest
steps.stepSummary: Quoting שמואל, רב נחמן says the souls of both רשעים and בינונים are handed to דומה. The בינונים have rest, and the רשעים do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: If I were already dead, I could not tell you this. This is what שמואל said: both these and those are handed over to דומה. These, the in-between, have rest. Those, the wicked, have no rest.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבה's question with a tradition from שמואל. First he remarks that it is good he is still alive to pass it on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בינונים share one thing with the רשעים: both are handed over to דומה, the angel in charge of the souls of the dead. But unlike the רשעים, the בינונים are not thrown around. They have rest.

keyTerms.meaning: The angel in charge of the souls of the dead

steps.confusionAlert: Who is 'אלו ואלו' (these and those)? It does not mean צדיקים and רשעים. It means the רשעים and the בינונים. The first 'הללו' (who have rest) refers to the בינונים.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Were I dead,
I would not be able to tell you this matter.
This is what Shmuel said:
These and those are handed over to Duma.
phrases.notes: These = the wicked and the middling people.

phrases.english: These (the middling) have rest.
Those (the wicked) do not have rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ לְדוּמָה נִמְסָרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The souls of בינונים are given to דומה like those of רשעים, but they have rest.
steps.whatToRemember: Three groups: צדיקים are stored under the כסא הכבוד. בינונים go to דומה and have rest. רשעים go to דומה and have no rest.

steps.title: רב מרי: even the bodies of the righteous become dust
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי says that even the bodies of צדיקים will eventually turn to dust, based on a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: The righteous will also become dust, as it is written, 'And the dust returns to the earth as it was.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי adds a new statement about the bodies of צדיקים. He says they do not stay whole forever. This sets up a discussion that continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said the bodies of צדיקים 'rest in peace.' Someone might think this means they never decay. רב מרי says no: the פסוק from step 5 ('the dust returns to the earth') applies to everyone, including צדיקים.

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
The righteous are destined to become dust,
as it is written: "And the dust returns
to the earth as it was."
phrases.notes: קהלת 12:7, the same פסוק used in step 5.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from souls back to bodies, limiting the 'rest in peace' idea of step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the bodies of צדיקים will eventually return to dust.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next part of the גמרא, which tests רב מרי's claim.

steps.title: Diggers disturb a grave on רב נחמן's land
steps.stepSummary: Diggers on רב נחמן's land are rebuked by the buried רב אחאי בר יאשיה. רב נחמן comes and asks who he is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some diggers were digging in רב נחמן's land. רב אחאי בר יאשיה, who was buried there, scolded them. They told רב נחמן that a man had scolded them. רב נחמן came and asked, 'Who are you, sir?' He answered, 'I am אחאי בר יאשיה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that tests רב מרי's teaching from the previous step. This is the setup: we meet a buried צדיק whose body is still whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מרי just said that even צדיקים become dust. Here is a צדיק who is still whole enough to speak and scold people. The rest of the story is a back-and-forth about how this can be.

keyTerms.meaning: He snorted at them, a sound of scolding
Who is the master? A polite way to ask 'Who are you?'

phrases.english: Those diggers
who were digging in the land of Rav Nachman.

phrases.aramaic: נְחַר בְּהוּ רַב אַחַאי בַּר יֹאשִׁיָּה.
phrases.english: Rav Achai bar Yoshiya snorted at them (rebuked them).
phrases.notes: He was buried there, and they disturbed his grave.

phrases.english: They came and said to Rav Nachman:
A man snorted at us.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאן נִיהוּ מָר?
phrases.english: He came and said to him: Who is the master?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא אַחַאי בַּר יֹאשִׁיָּה.
phrases.english: He said to him: I am Achai bar Yoshiya.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ קָפוֹלָאֵי דַּהֲווֹ קָפְלִי בְּאַרְעָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that seems to go against רב מרי's teaching in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buried צדיק, רב אחאי בר יאשיה, was found with his body still whole and able to speak.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks how his body is still whole
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges him: didn't רב מרי say that צדיקים will become dust?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: 'But didn't רב מרי say that the righteous will eventually become dust?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges רב אחאי with רב מרי's teaching from Step 16. If צדיקים turn to dust, how is his body still whole?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The conflict is now out in the open. רב מרי's teaching says a צדיק's body should become dust, yet here is one that has not.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְלָאו אָמַר רַב מָרִי:
phrases.english: He said to him: But didn't Rav Mari say:
The righteous are destined to become dust?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the teaching from Step 16 to challenge what is seen in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that רב אחאי's body is still whole
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב מרי taught that צדיקים become dust, so a whole body of a צדיק seems impossible.

steps.title: רב אחאי dismisses רב מרי's authority
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי answers: who is this מרי? I don't know him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'And who is מרי, whom I do not know?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי pushes the challenge away. He says רב מרי's opinion is not enough to prove anything to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not deal with the content of the teaching. He only rejects its authority, because רב מרי was a teacher he did not know. This forces רב נחמן to find a stronger source.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אחאי leaves out the title 'רב' and just says 'מרי.' As רש״י puts it, he means that he pays no attention to the words of a teacher he does not know.

phrases.english: He said to him: And who is Mari
whom I do not know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes away the challenge of Step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The authority of רב מרי's statement
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A statement from a teacher he does not know is not binding on him.

steps.title: רב נחמן brings a verse from קהלת
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן switches to a פסוק: 'and the dust returns to the earth as it was.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'But a פסוק is written: "And the dust returns to the earth as it was" (קהלת 12:7).'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן upgrades his challenge. Instead of quoting a person, he quotes a פסוק from קהלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the actual source of רב מרי's teaching. A פסוק cannot be brushed aside the way a person's opinion can, so רב אחאי must now give a real answer.

phrases.english: He said to him: But there is a verse written:
"And the dust returns to the earth as it was"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in Step 19 by bringing a פסוק instead of a person.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחאי's body still being whole
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says every body returns to dust, so his body should have turned to dust too.

steps.title: Bones of someone without envy do not rot
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי quotes משלי: envy rots the bones. Someone without envy keeps his bones whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Whoever taught you קהלת did not teach you משלי, where it is written, "Envy is the rotting of the bones" (משלי 14:30). Anyone who has envy in his heart, his bones rot. Anyone who has no envy in his heart, his bones do not rot.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי answers with a different פסוק. It shows that a person free of envy does not decay in the grave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in קהלת is a general rule. The פסוק in משלי adds an exception: the body decays because of קנאה. A person with no קנאה, like רב אחאי, keeps his bones whole.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who taught you to read

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a strong מוסר lesson: being free of envy brings even physical blessing that lasts after death.

phrases.english: He said to him: The one who taught you Kohelet
did not teach you Mishlei,
as it is written: "And envy is the rotting of the bones."

phrases.aramaic: כָּל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ קִנְאָה בְּלִבּוֹ —
phrases.english: Anyone who has envy in his heart,
his bones rot;
anyone who does not have envy in his heart,
his bones do not rot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פסוק from קהלת in Step 20 with a פסוק from משלי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the general פסוק with another פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every body, even a צדיק's, decays to dust.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person with no קנאה in his heart does not decay.

steps.title: רב נחמן feels his body and invites him inside
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן touches him, feels that he has a real body, and invites him into the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: He touched him and saw that he had real substance. He said to him: 'Let the master get up and come into the house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. רב נחמן checks for himself that the body is truly whole, then politely invites רב אחאי into his home. This sets up רב אחאי's next reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Touching him confirms that רב אחאי's answer about envy is really true. The invitation assumes the dead man could simply get up and leave his grave.

keyTerms.meaning: Substance, solid flesh you can feel

phrases.english: He touched him,
and saw that he had substance.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֵיקוּם מָר לְגַוֵּויהּ דְּבֵיתָא.
phrases.english: He said to him: Let the master arise and come into the house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms Step 21 by touch and moves the story forward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אחאי's body was confirmed to be solid, and he was invited to leave the grave.

steps.title: The dead may not leave until ה׳ opens the graves
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי refuses. He says רב נחמן hasn't even learned נביאים: only ה׳ opens the graves.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'You have shown that you have not even read נביאים, where it is written, "And you shall know that I am ה׳ when I open your graves" (יחזקאל 37:13).'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי turns down the invitation. He explains that the dead may not leave their graves on their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ה׳ is the one who opens the graves. So a dead person cannot get up before תחיית המתים, even if his body is whole. רב אחאי teases רב נחמן for missing a פסוק in נביאים too.

keyTerms.meaning: You have revealed your own mind, meaning you showed what you know

phrases.english: He said to him: You have revealed about yourself
that you have not even read the Prophets,
as it is written: "And you shall know that I am the Lord
when I open your graves."

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּלֵּית אַדַּעְתָּךְ דַּאֲפִילּוּ נְבִיאֵי לָא קְרֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the invitation of Step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that a dead person may get up and leave his grave
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Only ה׳ opens the graves, at תחיית המתים.

steps.title: רב נחמן brings a verse from the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges again: the תורה says 'to dust you shall return.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'But it is written: "For you are dust, and to dust you shall return" (בראשית 3:19).'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן comes back to the main question with a stronger source, a פסוק from the תורה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in משלי explained the פסוק in קהלת. But this פסוק in בראשית is said to all of mankind, so it seems that every body must become dust, envy or not.

phrases.english: He said to him: But isn't it written:
"For you are dust, and to dust you shall return"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב כִּי עָפָר אַתָּה וְאֶל עָפָר תָּשׁוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question of decay from Steps 18 and 20 and raises it with a פסוק from the תורה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 21 that a person free of envy does not decay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה says every person returns to dust, with no exception.

steps.title: Turning to dust happens one hour before resurrection
steps.stepSummary: רב אחאי answers: that פסוק happens to צדיקים only one hour before תחיית המתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'That פסוק applies one hour before תחיית המתים.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחאי settles the last question. צדיקים do return to dust, but only for a moment, right before the dead come back to life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both ideas fit together. A צדיק without envy stays whole in the grave for all the long years. He still fulfills 'to dust you shall return' just one hour before תחיית המתים, so he can be created anew (מהרש"א). This also explains רב מרי's statement that צדיקים will become dust: it happens at the very end.
steps.whatToRemember: A צדיק who has no קנאה stays whole in the grave. He becomes dust only one hour before תחיית המתים. So all the פסוקים are true, and רב מרי's teaching fits in as well.

phrases.english: He said to him: That verse applies
one hour before the resurrection of the dead.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא שָׁעָה אַחַת קוֹדֶם תְּחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from בראשית in Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting when the פסוק takes effect
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every body turns to dust and stays dust in the grave.
steps.terutzMaskana: For צדיקים without envy, turning to dust happens only one hour before תחיית המתים.

steps.title: A heretic asks how שמואל could be brought up from the dead
steps.stepSummary: A מין challenges רבי אבהו: if the souls of צדיקים are stored under the כסא הכבוד, how did the בעלת אוב bring up שמואל?
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain heretic said to רבי אבהו: You say that the souls of the righteous are stored away beneath the Throne of Glory. Then how did the necromancer bring up שמואל by necromancy?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story starts. A מין points out what looks like a contradiction in Jewish belief about the souls of צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jewish teaching is that a צדיק's soul is stored safely under the כסא הכבוד. But in שמואל א פרק כח, the בעלת אוב in עין דור brought up שמואל to speak with שאול. If his soul was locked away above, how could a necromancer reach it and bring it down?

keyTerms.meaning: A heretic or sectarian who argued against the Sages
The Throne of Glory, ה׳'s heavenly throne
The impure necromancer, meaning the בעלת אוב who supposedly raised the dead

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ:
phrases.english: A certain heretic said to Rabbi Abbahu:
You say that the souls of the righteous
are stored away beneath the Throne of Glory.
The impure necromancer,
phrases.notes: Refers to the בעלת אוב of עין דור (שמואל א כח).

phrases.english: how did she bring up Samuel by necromancy?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מִינָא לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story that challenges רבי אליעזר's teaching from step 12, that the souls of צדיקים are stored beneath the כסא הכבוד.
steps.kashyaTarget: The belief that souls of צדיקים are stored beneath the כסא הכבוד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the soul is stored above, a necromancer should not have been able to bring שמואל up. The story in שמואל א seems to contradict the belief.

steps.title: It happened within twelve months of שמואל's death
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that שאול's visit to the בעלת אוב was within twelve months of שמואל's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, it was within twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the מין: the event with שמואל took place within the first twelve months after he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו does not deny that souls of צדיקים are stored under the כסא הכבוד. He says that during the first twelve months the situation is different, so שמואל could still be brought up. The next step brings a ברייתא to prove this.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that case with שמואל
Twelve months, the first year after death

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ הֲוָה,
phrases.english: There, it was within twelve months.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the מין's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Time-based distinction: the rule applies after twelve months, and the שמואל story was before that.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מין assumed a צדיק's soul is stored above immediately after death, so no necromancer could reach it.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the first twelve months the soul still has contact with this world, so the שמואל story does not contradict the belief.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the soul goes up and down for twelve months
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that for twelve months the body remains and the soul rises and descends. After that, the body ceases to exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: For all twelve months his body remains, and his soul goes up and comes down. After twelve months, the body ceases to exist.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו brings a ברייתא as a source for his answer. Its last sentence continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that in the first year the body still exists and the soul moves back and forth between heaven and this world. That explains how שמואל could be brought up then. After twelve months the body is gone, and the next passage will explain what happens to the soul.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: "His body remains" does not mean the person is alive. It means the body has not yet decayed, and the soul still has a connection to it. The sentence "after twelve months the body ceases" is not finished here. It continues on the next amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: The twelve-month idea shows up elsewhere too, for example in the custom of saying קדיש and mourning for a parent for about a year.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ גּוּפוֹ קַיָּים,
phrases.english: For all twelve months his body remains,
and his soul goes up and comes down.

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ הַגּוּף בָּטֵל
phrases.english: After twelve months, the body ceases to exist
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבהו's twelve-month answer with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבהו's claim that the שמואל event was possible because it was within twelve months
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: for twelve months the body remains and the soul goes up and down.
